Given that the relativistic mass $m$ is related to rest mass $m_0$ by:
$$m = \frac{m_0}{\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}} = \frac{3}{2}m_0$$
$$\sqrt{1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}} = \frac{2}{3} \implies 1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2} = \frac{4}{9} \implies \frac{v}{c} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$$

By length contraction formula:
$$L = L_0 \sqrt{1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}}$$
Given rest length $L_0 = 1\text{ m}$:
$$L = 1 \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\text{ m} \approx 0.667\text{ m}$$
proTip: Length contraction only occurs along the direction of motion; dimensions perpendicular to motion remain unchanged.
